tasks.gr11-vectors-t1: Topic: Vectors and Forces. Cover resultant vectors (head-to-tail method, Pythagorean theorem for perpendicular vectors), vector resolution into horizontal and vertical components (F_x = F cosθ, F_y = F sinθ), drawing and interpreting free-body diagrams (FBDs), and calculating net force. Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate resultant magnitudes and directions using Pythagoras and trigonometry, resolve forces into components, sketch FBDs for objects on horizontal surfaces and inclined planes, and determine net force acting on a system.
tasks.gr11-work-energy-t1: Topic: Work, Energy and Power. Cover work done by a constant force (W = F·d·cosθ, unit: joule), kinetic energy (KE = ½mv²), gravitational potential energy (PE = mgh), the work-energy theorem (W_net = ΔKE), conservation of mechanical energy (KE + PE = constant when no friction acts), and power (P = W/Δt = Fv, unit: watt). Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate work done at various angles, apply the work-energy theorem, use conservation of mechanical energy to find speed or height, and calculate power output in mechanical systems.
tasks.gr11-newtons-laws-t1: Topic: Newton's Laws and Friction. Cover Newton's First Law (inertia: an object in equilibrium has zero net force), Newton's Second Law (F_net = ma as a vector equation in the direction of acceleration), Newton's Third Law (action-reaction pairs are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, and act on different objects), static friction (f_s ≤ μ_s × N) and kinetic friction (f_k = μ_k × N). Ask Grade 11 learners to identify action-reaction pairs, apply the second law to solve for acceleration or force, distinguish static from kinetic friction, solve inclined-plane problems, and draw and interpret force diagrams.
